literal: Book of Northern Qi, Volume 11 [1]
idiomatic: Book of Northern Qi, Volume 11 [1]

literal: Biographies, Third
idiomatic: Biographies 3

literal: The Six Princes of Wenxiang
idiomatic: The Six Princes of Wenxiang

literal: Prince Kangshu of Henan Xiaoyu; Prince of Guangning Xiaoheng; Prince of Hejian Xiaowan
idiomatic: Prince Kangshu of Henan (Xiaoyu); Prince of Guangning (Xiaoheng); Prince of Hejian (Xiaowan)

literal: Prince Wu of Lanling Xiaoguan; Prince of Ande Yanzong; Prince of Yuyang Shaoxin
idiomatic: Prince Wu of Lanling (Xiaoguan); Prince of Ande (Yanzong); Prince of Yuyang (Shaoxin)

literal: Wenxiang had six sons: Empress Yuan of Wenjing bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian; Lady Song bore Prince Xiaoyu of Henan; Lady Wang bore Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning; Prince Changgong of Lanling could not obtain his mother's surname; Lady Chen bore Prince Yanzong of Ande; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng had six sons: Empress Yuan of Wenjing bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian; Lady Song bore Prince Xiaoyu of Henan; Lady Wang bore Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning; Prince Changgong of Lanling never learned his mother's surname; Lady Chen bore Prince Yanzong of Ande; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang.

literal: Wucheng often had He Shikai and Empress Hu sit facing each other playing shuo; Xiaoyu remonstrated, saying, "The empress is mother to all under Heaven — she must not touch hands with a subordinate minister.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan often had He Shikai and Empress Hu sit facing each other playing shuo; Xiaoyu remonstrated, saying, "The empress is mother to all under Heaven — she must not touch hands with a subordinate minister.

literal: " The emperor took this deeply to heart.
idiomatic: " The emperor took this deeply to heart.

literal: Later he also said that the Prince of Zhao Commandery's father had died by violence and should not be kept close.
idiomatic: Later he also said that Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery's father had died by violence and should not be kept close.

literal: On this account both Rui and Shikai looked askance at him.
idiomatic: On this account both Gao Rui and He Shikai looked askance at him.

literal: Shikai secretly reported his extravagance and presumption; Rui also said that east of the mountains one heard only of the Prince of Henan, and never of Your Majesty.
idiomatic: He Shikai secretly reported his extravagance and presumption; Gao Rui also said that east of the mountains one heard only of the Prince of Henan, and never of the emperor.

literal: The emperor on this account came to resent him.
idiomatic: The emperor on this account came to resent him.

literal: An Erzhu palace woman named Monü had originally served the empress dowager; Xiaoyu had first had relations with her, and later, on the night of the crown prince's wedding, Xiaoyu stole away to speak with her.
idiomatic: An Erzhu palace woman named Monü had originally served the empress dowager; Xiaoyu had first had relations with her, and later, on the night of the crown prince's wedding, stole away to speak with her.

literal: Wucheng was greatly enraged and made him drink thirty-seven cups of wine in succession.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan was greatly enraged and made him drink thirty-seven cups of wine in succession.

literal: His body was extremely corpulent, his waistband ten arm-spans around.
idiomatic: His body was extremely corpulent, his waist ten arm-spans around.

literal: He had Lou Ziyan carry him out and poison him in the carriage.
idiomatic: He had Lou Ziyan carry him out and poison him in the carriage.

literal: At the West Flowery Gate he grew feverish and stifled with distress, threw himself into the water, and died.
idiomatic: At the West Flowery Gate he grew feverish and stifled with distress, threw himself into the water, and died.

literal: He was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

literal: His son Hongjie succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Hongjie succeeded.

literal: Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning was Wenxiang's second son.
idiomatic: Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning was Gao Cheng's second son.

literal: He rose in succession to Governor of Si Province, Chief Minister of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand General, and Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: He rose in succession to Governor of Si Province, Chief Minister of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand General, and Grand Marshal.

literal: Xiaoheng loved and appreciated men of talent; he studied the classics and histories, enjoyed composing literary pieces, and possessed artistic skill.
idiomatic: Xiaoheng loved and appreciated men of talent; he studied the classics and histories, enjoyed composing literary pieces, and possessed artistic skill.

literal: Once on the wall of his reception hall he painted an azure hawk himself; viewers all took it for real; he also made a painting of court gentlemen — both were marvels of the age.
idiomatic: Once on the wall of his reception hall he painted an azure hawk himself; viewers all took it for real. He also made a painting of court gentlemen — both were marvels of the age.

literal: When the Last Emperor fled in defeat from Jinyang to Ye, an edict summoned the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Light.
idiomatic: When the Last Emperor fled in defeat from Jinyang to Ye, an edict summoned the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Light.

literal: Xiaoheng said that with the great enemy already pressing deep, affairs must rely on swift adaptation.
idiomatic: Xiaoheng said that with the great enemy already pressing deep, affairs must rely on swift adaptation.

literal: The Prince of Rencheng should be sent to lead the Youzhou-route troops through Tumen Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Bing Province;
idiomatic: The Prince of Rencheng should be sent to lead the Youzhou-route troops through Tumen Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Bing Province;

literal: Dugu Yongye should lead the Luozhou troops toward Tong Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Chang'an;
idiomatic: Dugu Yongye should lead the Luozhou troops toward Tong Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Chang'an;

literal: your servant asks to lead the capital-region troops out through Fukou and advance with drums beating to meet the enemy.
idiomatic: your servant asks to lead the capital-region troops out through Fukou and advance with drums beating to meet the enemy.

literal: When the enemy heard that there were armies north and south, they would naturally scatter in rout.
idiomatic: When the enemy heard that there were armies north and south, they would naturally scatter in rout.

literal: He also asked that palace women and precious objects be brought out to reward the officers and soldiers; the emperor would not adopt this.
idiomatic: He also asked that palace women and precious objects be brought out to reward the officers and soldiers; the emperor would not adopt this.

literal: When Chengguang succeeded to the throne, Xiaoheng was made Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: When Chengguang succeeded to the throne, Xiaoheng was made Grand Preceptor.

literal: He joined with Huyan Zu, Moduolou Jingxian, and Wei Xiangyuan in a common plot, fixing the fifth day of the first month [2]: Xiaoheng was to behead Gao Anaogong at the Gate of a Thousand Autumns; Xiangyuan inside would respond with the forbidden guard; Zu and Jingxian would lead troops out from the Pleasure Garden.
idiomatic: He joined with Huyan Zu, Moduolou Jingxian, and Wei Xiangyuan in a common plot, fixing the fifth day of the first month [2]: Xiaoheng was to behead Gao Anaogong at the Gate of a Thousand Autumns; Xiangyuan inside would respond with the forbidden guard; Zu and Jingxian would lead troops out from the Pleasure Garden.

literal: Before long Anaogong took a shortcut from another residence into the palace, and the affair did not succeed.
idiomatic: Before long Anaogong took a shortcut from another residence into the palace, and the affair did not succeed.

literal: He then asked to go out to resist the western army, saying to Anaogong, Han Changluan, Chen Dexin, and the others, "The court will not grant permission to go out and strike the enemy — are you not afraid Xiaoheng will rebel?
idiomatic: He then asked to go out to resist the western army, saying to Anaogong, Han Changluan, Chen Dexin, and the others, "The court will not grant permission to go out and strike the enemy — are you not afraid Xiaoheng will rebel?

literal: If Xiaoheng defeats Yuwen Yong and then reaches Chang'an, what will rebellion have to do with the affairs of the state?
idiomatic: If Xiaoheng defeats Yuwen Yong and then reaches Chang'an, what will rebellion have to do with the affairs of the state?

literal: At today's urgent pass you still harbor such suspicions.
idiomatic: At today's urgent pass you still harbor such suspicions.

literal: " Gao and Han, fearing he might change, sent Xiaoheng out as Governor of Cang Province.
idiomatic: " Gao and Han, fearing he might change, sent Xiaoheng out as Governor of Cang Province.

literal: When he reached the province, he joined the Prince of Rencheng at Xindu with five thousand men to plan together for restoration.
idiomatic: When he reached the province, he joined the Prince of Rencheng at Xindu with five thousand men to plan together for restoration.

literal: Prince Xian of Zhou came to attack; their forces were weak and could not resist.
idiomatic: Prince Xian of Zhou came to attack; their forces were weak and could not resist.

literal: In anger he said, "Because of the petty man Gao Anaogong, my road is at an end!
idiomatic: In anger he said, "Because of the petty man Gao Anaogong, my road is at an end!

literal: " A Qi turncoat, Qi Fulinghe, stabbed Xiaoheng with a spear and knocked him from his horse; the slave Baize shielded him with his body; Xiaoheng still suffered wounds in several places and was then taken captive.
idiomatic: " A Qi turncoat, Qi Fulinghe, stabbed Xiaoheng with a spear and knocked him from his horse; the slave Baize shielded him with his body; Xiaoheng still suffered wounds in several places and was then taken captive.

literal: Prince Xian of Zhou asked Xiaoheng the reason for Qi's fall; Xiaoheng himself explained the state's calamity, words and tears together falling, his bearing composed in every movement.
idiomatic: Prince Xian of Zhou asked Xiaoheng the reason for Qi's fall; Xiaoheng himself explained the state's calamity, words and tears together falling, his bearing composed in every movement.

literal: Xian changed countenance on his account, personally washed his wounds and applied medicine, and treated him with great courtesy.
idiomatic: Xian changed countenance on his account, personally washed his wounds and applied medicine, and treated him with great courtesy.

literal: Xiaoheng sighed alone and said, "Li Mushu said the Qi house would last twenty-eight years — today it has indeed come to pass.
idiomatic: Xiaoheng sighed alone and said, "Li Mushu said the Qi house would last twenty-eight years — today it has indeed come to pass.

literal: Apart from the Shenwu Emperor, not one of my fathers and brothers among the clan reached forty — such is fate.
idiomatic: Apart from Gao Huan, not one of my fathers and brothers among the clan reached forty — such is fate.

literal: The succeeding ruler lacked independent insight; the chief ministers were no pillars to rely upon — I only regret that I could not grasp the tally of command, receive the plans of the temple, and give full play to the strength of my heart.
idiomatic: The succeeding ruler lacked independent insight; the chief ministers were no pillars to rely upon — I only regret that I could not grasp the tally of command, receive the plans of the temple, and give full play to the strength of my heart.

literal: " When he reached Chang'an, by precedent he was appointed Opener of the Way and Marquis of a county.
idiomatic: " When he reached Chang'an, by precedent he was appointed Opener of the Way and Marquis of a county.

literal: Later, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang, he feasted the Qi ruler and ministers, himself playing the barbarian pipa and ordering Xiaoheng to play the flute.
idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang, he feasted the Qi ruler and ministers, himself playing the barbarian pipa and ordering Xiaoheng to play the flute.

literal: He declined, saying, "The music of a fallen state is not worth hearing.
idiomatic: He declined, saying, "The music of a fallen state is not worth hearing.

literal: " Though pressed he obeyed; he raised the flute barely to his lips, tears falling in sobs, and Emperor Wu then stopped.
idiomatic: " Though pressed he obeyed; he raised the flute barely to his lips, tears falling in sobs, and Emperor Wu then stopped.

literal: In the tenth month of that year his illness grew severe; he petitioned to be buried back in Shandong, and permission was granted.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year his illness grew severe; he petitioned to be buried back in Shandong, and permission was granted.

literal: Before long he died; an order was issued to return his body for burial at Ye.
idiomatic: Before long he died; an order was issued to return his body for burial at Ye.

literal: Xiaowan, as Wenxiang's legitimate heir of the generation, was proud and self-important.
idiomatic: Xiaowan, as Gao Cheng's legitimate heir of the generation, was proud and self-important.

literal: At the Prince of Henan's death, the princes within the palace did not dare raise a sound; only Xiaowan wept loudly and went out.
idiomatic: At Prince Xiaoyu of Henan's death, the princes within the palace did not dare raise a sound; only Xiaowan wept loudly and went out.

literal: He also resented those in power and made a straw effigy which he shot at.
idiomatic: He also resented those in power and made a straw effigy which he shot at.

literal: He Shikai and Zu Ting slandered him, saying, "The straw effigy was modeled on the sacred person.
idiomatic: He Shikai and Zu Ting slandered him, saying, "The straw effigy was modeled on the sacred person.

literal: Moreover, when the Turks earlier came to the province, Xiaowan took off his helmet and cast it to the ground, saying, 'Am I an old woman that I must wear this?'
idiomatic: Moreover, when the Turks earlier came to the province, Xiaowan took off his helmet and cast it to the ground, saying, 'Am I an old woman that I must wear this?'

literal: These words were directed at Your Majesty.
idiomatic: These words were directed at Your Majesty.

literal: " Earlier, in Wei times there was a rhyme: "Henan plants grain, Hebei gives birth; on the white poplar's crown a golden cock crows.
idiomatic: " Earlier, in Wei times there was a rhyme: "Henan plants grain, Hebei gives birth; on the white poplar's crown a golden cock crows.

literal: " Ting used this to explain, saying, "Henan and Hebei mean Hejian.
idiomatic: " Ting used this to explain, saying, "Henan and Hebei mean Hejian.

literal: The golden cock's crow means Xiaowan will build a golden cock and proclaim a great amnesty.
idiomatic: The golden cock's crow means Xiaowan will build a golden cock and proclaim a great amnesty.

literal: " The emperor was quite swayed.
idiomatic: " The emperor was quite swayed.

literal: At the time Xiaowan had obtained a Buddha tooth and placed it in his residence; at night there was divine light.
idiomatic: At the time Xiaowan had obtained a Buddha tooth and placed it in his residence; at night there was divine light.

literal: Fashun of Zhaoxuan Abbey asked to report it to the throne [3]; he would not consent.
idiomatic: Fashun of Zhaoxuan Abbey asked to report it to the throne [3]; he would not consent.

literal: When the emperor heard of it, he sent men to search the residence and found several hundred spears and banners from the arsenal.
idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he sent men to search the residence and found several hundred spears and banners from the arsenal.

literal: When the emperor heard of this, he took it for rebellion.
idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he took it for rebellion.

literal: His concubines were interrogated; one surnamed Chen, who had no favor, falsely answered that "Xiaowan painted the emperor's likeness and wept before it" — but in truth it was a portrait of Wenxiang, before which Xiaowan often wept.
idiomatic: His concubines were interrogated; one surnamed Chen, who had no favor, falsely answered that "Xiaowan painted the emperor's likeness and wept before it" — but in truth it was a portrait of Gao Cheng, before which Xiaowan often wept.

literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered the guard Helian Fuxuan to beat him with an inverted whip.
idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered the guard Helian Fuxuan to beat him with an inverted whip.

literal: Xiaowan cried out "Uncle!" The emperor in anger said, "Who is your uncle?
idiomatic: Xiaowan cried out "Uncle!" The emperor in anger said, "Who is your uncle?

literal: You dare call me uncle!
idiomatic: You dare call me uncle!

literal: " Xiaowan said, "Grandson of Emperor Shenwu, son of Emperor Wenxiang, nephew of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei — why may I not call you uncle?
idiomatic: " Xiaowan said, "Grandson of Gao Huan, son of Gao Cheng, nephew of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei — why may I not call you uncle?

literal: " The emperor grew still more enraged and broke both his shins, and he died.
idiomatic: " The emperor grew still more enraged and broke both his shins, and he died.

literal: He was buried on the western hills; after the emperor's death he was reinterred.
idiomatic: He was buried on the western hills; after the emperor's death he was reinterred.

literal: His son Zhengli succeeded; in youth he was clever and sharp, and could recite the Zuo Tradition.
idiomatic: His son Zhengli succeeded; in youth he was clever and sharp, and could recite the Zuo Tradition.

literal: When Qi fell he was transferred to Mian Prefecture, where he died.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he was transferred to Mian Prefecture, where he died.

literal: Prince Wu of Lanling, Changgong — also named Xiaoguan — was Wenxiang's fourth son.
idiomatic: Prince Wu of Lanling, Changgong — also named Xiaoguan — was Gao Cheng's fourth son.

literal: He was promoted in succession to Governor of Bing Province.
idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Governor of Bing Province.

literal: When the Turks entered Jinyang, Changgong exerted himself to the utmost in striking them.
idiomatic: When the Turks entered Jinyang, Changgong exerted himself to the utmost in striking them.

literal: At the defeat at Mang Mountain [4], Changgong served as central army commander; leading five hundred horsemen he entered the Zhou army a second time and reached beneath the walls of Jinyong; besieged in extreme peril, those on the walls did not recognize him; Changgong removed his helmet to show his face, and only then did they lower crossbowmen to rescue him — whereupon there was a great victory.
idiomatic: At the defeat at Mang Mountain [4], Changgong served as central army commander; leading five hundred horsemen he entered the Zhou army a second time and reached beneath the walls of Jinyong; besieged in extreme peril, those on the walls did not recognize him; Changgong removed his helmet to show his face, and only then did they lower crossbowmen to rescue him — whereupon there was a great victory.

literal: The warriors together sang ballads of it — this is the Entry of the Prince of Lanling into Battle.
idiomatic: The warriors together sang ballads of it — this is the Entry of the Prince of Lanling into Battle.

literal: He served in succession as Governor of Si Province and of Qing and Ying provinces, and rather accepted goods and wealth.
idiomatic: He served in succession as Governor of Si Province and of Qing and Ying provinces, and rather accepted goods and wealth.

literal: Later he became Grand Commandant; with Duan Shao he attacked Baigu, and again attacked Dingyang.
idiomatic: Later he became Grand Commandant; with Duan Shao he attacked Baigu, and again attacked Dingyang.

literal: Shao fell ill; Changgong took overall command of his forces.
idiomatic: Shao fell ill; Changgong took overall command of his forces.

literal: Before and after, for military merit he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Julu, Changle, Leping, Gaoyang, and other commanderies.
idiomatic: Before and after, for military merit he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Julu, Changle, Leping, Gaoyang, and other commanderies.

literal: After the victory at Mang Mountain, the Last Emperor said to Changgong, "You entered the battle line too deeply; if it had gone badly, regret would have availed nothing.
idiomatic: After the victory at Mang Mountain, the Last Emperor said to Changgong, "You entered the battle line too deeply; if it had gone badly, regret would have availed nothing.

literal: " He replied, "Family affairs touch one closely — without noticing it, I did so.
idiomatic: " He replied, "Family affairs touch one closely — without noticing it, I did so.

literal: " The emperor resented his speaking of family affairs and on this account came to be wary of him.
idiomatic: " The emperor resented his speaking of family affairs and on this account came to be wary of him.

literal: When he was at Dingyang, his subordinate Wei Xiangyuan said to him, "Your Highness has received the court's commission — how can you be so greedy and cruel?
idiomatic: When he was at Dingyang, his subordinate Wei Xiangyuan said to him, "Your Highness has received the court's commission — how can you be so greedy and cruel?

literal: " Changgong did not reply.
idiomatic: " Changgong did not reply.

literal: Xiangyuan said, "Is it not because of the great victory at Mang Mountain — fearing that your martial prestige would excite jealousy, and wishing to defile yourself?
idiomatic: Xiangyuan said, "Is it not because of the great victory at Mang Mountain — fearing that your martial prestige would excite jealousy, and wishing to defile yourself?

literal: " Changgong said, "It is so.
idiomatic: " Changgong said, "It is so.

literal: " Xiangyuan said, "If the court resents Your Highness, for this offense it ought at once to punish you — seeking fortune instead hastens disaster.
idiomatic: " Xiangyuan said, "If the court resents Your Highness, for this offense it ought at once to punish you — seeking fortune instead hastens disaster.

literal: " Changgong wept; going forward on his knees he asked for a method to preserve himself.
idiomatic: " Changgong wept; going forward on his knees he asked for a method to preserve himself.

literal: Xiangyuan said, "Your Highness already had merit before; now you report victory again — your martial renown is too heavy; you ought to plead illness and remain at home, and not take part in affairs.
idiomatic: Xiangyuan said, "Your Highness already had merit before; now you report victory again — your martial renown is too heavy; you ought to plead illness and remain at home, and not take part in affairs.

literal: " Changgong agreed with his words but could not withdraw.
idiomatic: " Changgong agreed with his words but could not withdraw.

literal: When bandits harried the Jiang-Huai region, fearing he would again be made a general, he sighed and said, "Last year my face swelled — why does it not break out now?
idiomatic: When bandits harried the Jiang-Huai region, fearing he would again be made a general, he sighed and said, "Last year my face swelled — why does it not break out now?

literal: " From then on he had an illness and would not treat it.
idiomatic: " From then on he had an illness and would not treat it.

literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Wuping, the emperor had Xu Zhifan make him drink poison.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Wuping, the emperor had Xu Zhifan make him drink poison.

literal: Changgong said to his consort Lady Zheng, "I served the ruler with loyalty — what crime have I against Heaven, that I should meet poison?
idiomatic: Changgong said to his consort Lady Zheng, "I served the ruler with loyalty — what crime have I against Heaven, that I should meet poison?

literal: " The consort said, "Why do you not ask to see the imperial countenance?
idiomatic: " The consort said, "Why do you not ask to see the imperial countenance?
